subject.title: Session context bloat: bootstrap files re-injected every turn, wasting 20-30% tokens

question: Should OpenClaw change the global bootstrap-injection default from `always` to `continuation-skip`, while preserving explicit `always`, and defer MEMORY.md lazy loading plus configurable cache ordering to separate scoped work?
rationale: The present behavior is an intentional configuration default with compatibility implications, and the proposed memory and cache changes add distinct user-facing policies rather than repairing one mechanically defined defect.

options.title: Adopt safer continuation default
options.body: Change the implicit default to `continuation-skip`, preserve explicit `always`, and require upgrade-focused proof across normal, restart, heartbeat, lightweight, and compaction paths.

options.title: Keep explicit opt-in
options.body: Retain `always` as the default and improve documentation or diagnostics so cost-sensitive operators can enable continuation skipping deliberately.

options.title: Redesign bootstrap policy first
options.body: Pause the default change until maintainers choose a unified policy for memory loading, restart persistence, and prompt-cache boundaries.

recommendation.title: Adopt safer continuation default
recommendation.body: Change the implicit default to `continuation-skip`, preserve explicit `always`, and require upgrade-focused proof across normal, restart, heartbeat, lightweight, and compaction paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work is directly on the bootstrap prompt-routing surface where the compatibility decision would land.
